rows.name: Constellation Software Inc.
rows.last_memo: Constellation's stock jumped about 6.5% today with no apparent reason — no earnings, no acquisition news, no management update. For a company like this, where what matters is whether management keeps buying good software businesses at attractive prices and compounding free cash f

rows.name: Deckers Outdoor Corp.
rows.last_memo: Deckers had a decent but not exceptional quarter—sales grew about 6%, the direct-to-consumer business (selling straight to shoppers, bypassing retailers) grew a healthy 13%, and international demand kept building. The downside is that spending on overhead and marketing grew much
risks: SG&A growing at 2.2x the rate of revenue in Q1 FY27; if this reflects a higher-cost operating model rather than investment spending, operating margins could structurally compress by 200-300bps versus thesis assumptions.

Inventory rose $320M in the quarter to $807.6M—a seasonal build but the absolute level warrants monitoring against sell-through data; any buildup into fiscal year-end would be a kill-criterion proximity signal.

Operating lease commitments surged ($120M of new ROU assets in one quarter vs. $45M prior year), indicating a significant retail or distribution footprint expansion; lease costs are fixed obligations that increase operating leverage in a downturn.
Tariff uncertainty explicitly mentioned in forward-looking statements; as a footwear company with overseas manufacturing, any sustained tariff escalation could structurally raise COGS.

rows.name: Meta Platforms Inc.
rows.last_memo: A New Mexico court ordered Meta to pay $567 million for failing to protect children on Facebook and Instagram, and also told the company to change how it handles teen users on those platforms. The fine itself is small — Meta generates roughly $46 billion in cash per year, so this
risks: Mandated teen-protection product overhauls may restrict ad load and data collection on under-18 users across Facebook and Instagram, creating a measurable but currently unquantified revenue drag.

New Mexico ruling may embolden other U.S. states or federal regulators to pursue similar child safety actions, creating a patchwork of compliance obligations that raises operating complexity and cost.

Reputational damage from public child safety rulings could accelerate legislative momentum for federal children's online privacy or safety legislation that imposes structural limits on Meta's business model.
AI infrastructure capex at $64–72B annualized may become a floor rather than a ceiling if competitive AI spending escalates, permanently raising Meta's capital intensity above historical norms.

rows.name: International Business Machines Corporation
rows.last_memo: IBM just got permission to sell its Maximo software — which helps large organizations manage buildings, equipment, and physical assets — to U.S. federal government agencies. Previously, a missing government security certification blocked these sales entirely. This is genuinely go
risks: Federal procurement cycles are notoriously slow; FedRAMP authorization may not translate to meaningful revenue for 2-3 years, creating an execution timing gap.
Competing asset management vendors (ServiceNow, Oracle, SAP) may also pursue or already hold FedRAMP certifications, limiting IBM's first-mover window.

If the top-line miss reflects software or Red Hat deceleration rather than consulting/infrastructure, the primary growth engine of the thesis is impaired — this must be confirmed or ruled out via segment data.
Net debt/EBITDA at 3.47x remains above the 2.5x discipline threshold; any FCF guidance reduction would tighten this constraint materially.

rows.name: Amazon Com Inc.
rows.last_memo: Amazon's cloud boss said that essentially all of their AI server capacity is already committed to customers through 2028 — think of it like a hotel where every room is booked years in advance. This is important because one of the biggest questions about Amazon has been whether co
risks: Execution risk on supply side: if Amazon cannot build data center and AI chip capacity fast enough to honor multi-year commitments, customer satisfaction and contract terms could be impaired.

Concentration risk: capacity locked through 2028 means AWS is betting heavily on AI workloads remaining on current architectural assumptions — a disruptive shift in AI compute paradigm (e.g., dramatically more efficient models) could strand infrastructure investment.
Memory price inflation adding ~$20B to the capex program creates a near-term FCF headwind that could persist through 2026-2027 depending on DRAM/HBM market conditions.

Long-term debt doubled from $65.6B to $128.9B in six months (H1 2026 new issuance of ~$67B); while net debt/EBITDA remains well below 2.5x given earnings scale, the leverage trajectory warrants monitoring.

rows.name: Alphabet Inc.
rows.last_memo: Alphabet just borrowed $25 billion — the largest bond deal in its history — to fund the massive data centers and chips needed to compete in AI. This sounds alarming, but Alphabet has so much cash and generates so much profit that this doesn't create a financial stress problem. Th
risks: If AI infrastructure returns disappoint, Alphabet will have permanently increased its capital base and interest burden with limited ability to quickly reverse the commitment.
Debt issuance signals that organic FCF may be insufficient to simultaneously fund peak AI capex AND sustain the current buyback program — one or both may need to be reduced.
The 'AI arms race' framing suggests capex is partly competitive/defensive rather than purely return-driven, which is a lower-quality use of capital.

If AI infrastructure investment continues to scale faster than FCF generation, Alphabet could transition from a net-cash to a net-debt company within 2-3 years, potentially constraining capital return flexibility.

rows.name: NVIDIA Corporation
rows.last_memo: Reports say NVIDIA may be helping to finance OpenAI's purchase of NVIDIA hardware — essentially lending money to a customer to buy your own products. On one hand, this shows just how central NVIDIA is to the AI world: the most important AI company apparently wants NVIDIA's chips
risks: Vendor financing of GPU purchases, if confirmed and material, introduces credit concentration risk to NVIDIA's balance sheet tied to OpenAI's financial health.
A pattern of vendor-financed demand would raise questions about whether AI infrastructure capex is as organically robust as current revenue growth implies.
Reputational and regulatory risk if the financing arrangement is structured in a way that regulators view as anticompetitive or as a mechanism to lock OpenAI into NVIDIA exclusively.

If Google's chip achieves commercial-scale deployment with verified 10x inference cost reduction, it could accelerate hyperscaler substitution of NVIDIA GPUs for inference workloads, compressing both volumes and ASPs in the fastest-growing AI compute segment.

rows.name: Microsoft Corporation
rows.last_memo: A news headline says Microsoft made some kind of controversial AI decision, but the actual article content wasn't included, so we have no idea what happened. Reacting to a headline without knowing what's underneath it would be irresponsible. The business itself remains one of the
risks: Unknown AI strategic decision may affect Copilot pricing, partnership structure, or product roadmap — cannot quantify until details are available.
If the 'controversial decision' relates to OpenAI partnership terms or exclusivity arrangements, it could affect Azure AI differentiation — requires verification.

If AI-specific package targeting escalates, enterprise customers may impose stricter controls on open-source dependencies, marginally slowing developer adoption of Microsoft AI tooling on GitHub/Azure.

Repeated supply-chain incidents on npm could provide competitive ammunition for GitLab, JFrog Artifactory, or other alternative artifact registries seeking to displace GitHub in enterprise environments.

rows.name: Shopify Inc.
rows.last_memo: Shopify reported a better-than-expected quarter with strong sales growth and solid profit, driven by merchants processing more transactions through the platform. The company is also leaning hard into AI as a way to make its tools more powerful for merchants, which is a smart defe
risks: AI commerce strategy adds execution risk: if Shopify is investing heavily in AI tooling to stay ahead, this may pressure near-term margins or require capital allocation that delays FCF margin expansion.

AI-native commerce platforms (e.g., those building directly on LLM infrastructure) could bypass traditional storefront software entirely — the Q2 call highlights this is on management's radar, suggesting competitive intensity is real.
Valuation-to-fair-value gap (current price ~16x base case fair value) means any miss or guidance cut would cause severe price dislocations, even if the long-term thesis remains intact.
A 17% single-day move compresses the margin of safety further on an already premium valuation, making the stock more sensitive to any future guidance miss.

rows.name: Palantir Tech Inc.
rows.last_memo: Palantir's stock jumped nearly 30% in a single day, but no news about the actual business — new contracts, earnings, or AI platform wins — appears to explain it. The company itself is the same business it was yesterday: a high-quality AI software platform with real and growing ca
risks: At 63x trailing sales, any deceleration in commercial or government revenue growth — even a modest miss — could trigger a violent de-rating, creating forced-seller dynamics that affect even long-term holders who are psychologically anchored to recent prices.

A move of this magnitude without a disclosed catalyst suggests potential speculative or options-driven activity; if that flow reverses, the stock could give back gains equally rapidly, testing conviction without any change in fundamentals.
Revenue growth comparison base becomes extremely difficult in H2 2026 and 2027, increasing risk of apparent deceleration that could compress the multiple even if absolute growth remains strong.
Customer I represents 27% of accounts receivable — concentration risk at the AR level is elevated and warrants monitoring for any single-customer slowdown.

rows.name: Unitedhealth Group Inc.
rows.last_memo: The government is eliminating a subsidy that helped keep Medicare drug plan premiums low, and it takes effect in 2027. UnitedHealth runs one of the largest pharmacy benefit managers (Optum Rx), which depends heavily on Medicare drug plan economics, so this policy change hits a co
risks: Medicare Part D plan economics worsen materially in 2027 if UNH cannot reprice premiums fast enough to offset subsidy loss, pressuring both insurance and Optum pharmacy margins simultaneously.
Political framing of PBM subsidies as 'bailouts' increases the probability of further PBM-targeted legislation or CMS rulemaking adverse to Optum Rx's spread-based economics.
Senior member attrition from higher Part D premiums could reduce Optum's pharmacy dispensing volumes, adding a volume headwind on top of the margin headwind.
Federal removal of Medicare drug plan subsidy creates a structural cost shift onto Part D plan sponsors, compressing pharmacy segment margins from 2026 onward.

rows.name: AST SpaceMobile Inc.
rows.last_memo: AST SpaceMobile just added three of Europe's biggest phone carriers — Vodafone, Deutsche Telekom, and Orange — as partners, and got government approval to operate its satellite phone service in Japan. Think of this as getting shelf space in major stores before your product offici
risks: Accelerated European and Japanese expansion could increase near-term capex and launch cadence requirements, straining the already-negative FCF trajectory if satellite production does not scale on schedule.

Managing commercial rollout across multiple Tier-1 carriers in multiple jurisdictions simultaneously increases operational complexity and potential for execution misses that damage multiple partner relationships at once.

A Meta association — however informal — could raise competitive sensitivity if Meta pursues its own satellite connectivity strategy (e.g., via Starlink or proprietary infrastructure), potentially displacing ASTS from hyperscaler consideration.

Rapid constellation build-up ahead of beta service increases pressure on management to demonstrate revenue conversion quickly, raising market expectations that could punish any beta service disappointment.

rows.name: Tesla Inc.
rows.last_memo: Three things happened: European regulators quietly agreed to keep Tesla's self-driving safety data secret (apparently after Tesla pushed for that); Waymo's CEO publicly said Tesla's approach to self-driving — cameras only, no radar-like lidar sensors — is risky compared to how Wa
risks: European regulators may impose public safety-data disclosure requirements on Tesla's FSD/AV systems, potentially exposing adverse performance data and delaying commercial deployment timelines.
If lidar-inclusive safety standards become a regulatory norm in key markets, Tesla's camera-only AV architecture would face costly redesign or market exclusion.
The Optimus 1M-unit target, if repeatedly cited without operational follow-through, risks becoming a credibility liability rather than an asset — similar to prior Tesla production promises.

If Tesla's 'no user overrides' philosophy slows near-term FSD adoption by consumers who prefer configurable safety controls, subscription attach rates could disappoint in the medium term before the underlying AI reaches full trustworthiness.
